articles.description: Ban on illegal artisanal mining triggers mass exodus and diplomatic tensions with neighbouring Sahel states In the border town of Kourémalé, split between Guinea and Mali, thousands of families have been trudging across the frontier over the past week after a sudden ban on illegal artisanal mining triggered a wave of displacement and a regional diplomatic dispute. Some, like Seydou Traore, a miner in his 30s from Burkina Faso, made the 78-mile trek from Kourémalé to Ouezzindougou, farther inward. Last week, he gathered a small bundle of his belongings and fled Guinea after security forces ordered him and fellow miners to leave. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘I’m not ready to go to jail’: co-founder of Egypt’s last independent media outlet faces prison
articles.description: Mada Masr, the news site co-founded by Lina Attalah just before the 2013 military coup, is fighting for its life after being shut down, but its journalists have not given up hope Facing a year in prison for running Egypt’s leading independent news outlet Mada Masr , Lina Attalah is trying to focus on the everyday: waking at dawn to hear the birds sing before Cairo’s streets come alive and visiting Mada Masr’s shuttered offices with her reporters to water the plants and feed their four cats. Attalah is the reluctant face of Egypt’s embattled independent press at a moment of crisis. In the last six weeks, Egyptian authorities have waged a renewed crackdown on the few remaining independent media outlets left in the country, beginning with the arrest of the entire newsroom of the factchecking website Matsadaash. Continue reading...

articles.description: Inaugural parliamentary session comes as ousted populist Aleksandar Vučić threatens mass protests of his own Candidates for Serbia’s Student List, the grassroots movement of political outsiders that pulled off a spectacular victory in last month’s elections over the party of the populist leader Aleksandar Vučić, are to be sworn in as MPs as they begin the process of forming a government. The 140 candidates – among them academics, lawyers, scientists and the odd actor – will be sworn in on Tuesday during the inaugural session of the new parliament, bringing 14 years of rule by Vučić and his Serbian Progressive party (SNS) to an end. Continue reading...

articles.title: TV tonight: the extraordinary story of the Jewish refugee boy who became a CIA spy
articles.description: This Storyville film talks to Peter Sichel, who fled Nazi Germany, then became the CIA’s first station chief in Berlin. Plus: Stacey & Joe go camping. Here’s what to watch this evening 10pm, BBC Four Some people are blessed with interesting lives, others are cursed with them. It’s hard to say which category Peter Sichel falls into, but he lived quite a story and managed to tell it in this documentary, shortly before his death, aged 102. As a child, he fled Nazi Germany for the US. He later landed at the CIA and played a role in some of the late-20th century’s pivotal events. His critique of US foreign policy during that era is forensic and fascinating. Phil Harrison Continue reading...

articles.title: Heysel 85 review – rage-filled denunciation of the incompetence that fuelled a football disaster
articles.description: Teodora Ana Mihai and her passionately committed cast reconstruct the grim sequence of bad judgments that led to 39 fans dying Shame and rage are the keynotes of this immersive, viscerally powerful drama-thriller set amid the macabre tragedy of football’s 1985 European Cup final between Juventus and Liverpool in the crumbling Heysel stadium in Brussels. Crowd disorder before kickoff in a poorly maintained, badly policed venue resulted in the deaths of 39 fans. In this film, the roar of the crowd echoing overhead through the stadium’s claustrophobic tunnels is like the wailing of the damned, while the sport’s officer class flinch and panic as if at a wartime loss. Grimly, the match was allowed to go ahead, despite the fatalities; the authorities believed the game itself would restore order on a bread-and-circuses basis, and that abandoning the match would only cause greater violence and chaos. Heysel 85 is directed and co-written by Romanian-born and Belgian-based film-maker Teodora Ana Mihai; she is a former collaborator of Cristian Mungiu, though maybe the influence here is more Paul Greengrass. The film-makers have been criticised for fictionalising aspects: the players are depic

articles.title: The Brightness by Chad Harbach review – an ambitious sequel to The Art of Fielding
articles.description: Fifteen years on, this expansive follow-up to the campus epic explores female agency, friendship – and the messiness of early adulthood Back in 2011, Chad Harbach’s debut The Art of Fielding was hailed as the next Great American Novel. Set on the campus of Westish, a fictional midwestern liberal arts college, and steeped in baseball, it grappled with the big, quintessentially American themes – ambition, failure, the pursuit of perfection – that have traditionally been the genre’s hallmark. Harbach himself winkingly invited the categorisation: The Art of Fielding communes directly with the spirit of Herman Melville, arguably the greatest Great American Novelist of them all. Westish College, the novel explains, has claimed Melville as its own since the discovery of a lecture he gave there in 1880: its baseball team is known as the Harpooners; and a Melville statue presides over the campus like the genius of the place. Legend has it that Harbach laboured over The Art of Fielding for more than a decade. When it finally emerged, a feverish bidding war saw it sell for more than $650,000 (£431,000), a saga chronicled at length in Vanity Fair. Any follow-up to such a high-profile debut, le

articles.title: Belonging by Sonia Gandhi review – India’s elder stateswoman breaks her silence
articles.description: The Italian who became kingmaker in the world’s largest democracy charts her remarkable journey By any measure, it is one of the most extraordinary political stories of our age: a shy Italian girl locks eyes with the scion of an Indian political family, falls instantly and steadfastly in love, “transplanting herself” as a result, suffers soul-shattering tragedies, then takes the reins of power in the world’s largest democracy. It is a life that spans the extremes of privilege and distress, and half a century of seismic national history. No wonder publishers have been keen to secure the memoirs of the famously guarded Sonia Gandhi, soon to turn 80. Yet when the chance came, the deal with the country’s biggest publisher, Penguin Random House India, fell through at the last minute over what it termed “an impasse over a particular issue” in the text, with HarperCollins stepping into the breach. For those unfamiliar with the sensitive political context, the Nehru-Gandhi family has been in charge of India for about half the eight decades since independence – and the principal opposition to Narendra Modi’s prickly BJP regime for the past 12 years. Continue reading...

articles.title: The play that changed my life: ‘John Berger’s Pig Earth became something magical – they licked milk off bodies’
articles.description: The Three Lives of Lucie Cabrol by Complicité conjured the struggles of a French village with an intense rawness There are many things you see that are impactful, but few you can genuinely say change your life. I saw Complicité’s The Three Lives of Lucie Cabrol aged 16 on a school trip to Riverside Studios in London and it really reached me. I’d been educated in a very language, words-based way. Here the story was told – with such intensity! – through people’s bodies. The world they were conjuring, from a story by John Berger in his book Pig Earth, was about this remote French village – a world of labour. And the strife and struggles of these characters was expressed through the physical work of the company. Giant can be seen in cinemas from 19 November As told to Lindesay Irvine Continue reading...

articles.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the bedbugs that bit me – and worried Jake Gyllenhaal
articles.description: An infestation at my hotel meant my clothes had to be fumigated. When I turned up in shorts to interview the actor, he lent me his jacket, but I suspect he may have regretted it The biting flies were wild in Toronto in September 2012. A colleague and I were there to cover the film festival, but our key reference that year was a zinger from the 2007 cartoon Bee Movie, when it turns out Chris Rock’s mosquito has become a lawyer: “I was already a bloodsucking parasite,” he says, “all I needed was a briefcase!” (Bee Movie is one of the most brilliant and adult children’s movies ever; its central premise compares the honey industry to concentration camps.) Anyway, I spent the first week getting ever more bloodless and lumpy. We even shot a video about them, spraying repellent in front of us like Mace. It didn’t work. Every morning I woke bumpier than before. Continue reading...

articles.title: Is this Britain’s most beautiful bus journey? The Welsh service that beats the train hands down
articles.description: A new coach service between Holyhead in the north and Carmarthen in the south offers a thrilling glimpse of west Wales, from mountain peaks to pretty seafronts – and it knocks half an hour off the journey As anyone who has ever tried to catch a train from north to south Wales will know, it’s quite the adventure, and by adventure, I mean chore. You leave Wales, dip into England and then back into Wales to complete the journey. The fastest “Marches” route, which includes stops in Chester, Crewe and Shrewsbury, takes about five and a half hours and costs about £105, depending on your ticket. There are lots of reasons for this: mid-Wales has some challenging topography; the old rail networks, before the Beeching cuts, predominantly bled outwards, transporting slate, coal and steel to distant ports and markets. Last month, all that changed. Just not in the way you probably imagine. Continue reading...

articles.title: Sami Tamimi’s recipes for lamb and quince tagine with maftoul
articles.description: Falling-apart-tender lamb with jewelled, nutty bulgur wheat is a riot of texture and flavour These dishes were made to sit together. The lamb is slowly cooked with quince and saffron, bringing richness, warmth and a gentle sweetness, while the maftoul offers a lighter contrast with its lemon, currants and toasted almonds, and provides the perfect base for the fragrant meat juices. It’s a generous combination; simple enough for a family meal, but special enough to share with friends. Continue reading...

articles.title: India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes
articles.description: As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here The 13th-century Persian scholar Zakariyya al-Qazwini never travelled to India. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”. For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge. India has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. This has shaped how the country is perceived from afar, but it can often flatten its complexities. Continue reading...

articles.title: Belfast Flood Alleviation Scheme Sept 14-18
articles.description: Belfast Tidal Flood Alleviation Scheme Training Exercise A training exercise to install the temporary defences will take place between 14 – 18 September 2026. This year the locations are: Harbour Estate Sydenham (Greggs Quay to The O2 Belfast) Sydenham (Pottinger's Quay) Ravenhill As part of the exercise, the slip road from Ravenhill Road to the Albert Bridge will be closed overnight between 11pm and 6am on Wednesday 16 September. If required , the closure may also be in place on Thursday 17 September again overnight between 11pm and 6am. Diversion signage will be provided, directing city centre-bound traffic via Bridge End and Queen's Bridge. There may also be some short-term disruption and temporary footpath closures at other locations. Advisory signs will be provided where necessary, including along the towpath. The Department would like to thank the public in advance for their patience. Further details, including locations and programme, are available at: Belfast Tidal Flood Alleviation Scheme | Department for Infrastructure .

articles.title: NI Water Works - Cornagrade Road Enniskillen 3 Aug
articles.description: Essential Water Infrastructure Improvement Work gets underway – Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen NI Water is set to commence an upgrade of the water infrastructure on Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen in early August for approximately 6 weeks. The work will see around 400m of new watermain being laid along Cornagrade Road, starting at Cherrymount Roundabout on Monday 3 rd August and progressing as far as the second entrance to Kilmacormick Road. To facilitate the laying of this new watermain, a lane closure will be in place around each working area and signage will be in place. Working areas will be kept as short as possible (around 100m) with temporary traffic lights in place to manage the flow of traffic. Access to residential and business properties on and adjacent to Cornagrade Road will be available at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be affected for a short period of time while the pipelaying passes. Any bus stop located within a working area will be temporarily relocated.

articles.title: Derry - NIW Scheme - Racecourse Rd - from 27 July
articles.description: Essential water network upgrade to get underway on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett NI Water is set to begin an essential watermain upgrade on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett (Derry/Londonderry) on Monday 27 th July to improve the resilience of the local water supply network. The work, which involves laying around 170 metres of new watermain between Carnhill Roundabout and Greenhaw Road, will replace a section of the 50-year-old Ballyarnett Water Trunkmain which has been prone to bursts. The upgrade will help to protect homes from flooding, should a burst occur in the future, and provide improved access for NI Water maintenance. A l ane closure controlled by temporary traffic lights will be in place on Racecourse Road around the working area from Monday 27 th July for four weeks. A further two weeks of work will take place in the adjacent verge which will not require any traffic management. Temporary traffic lights will be manned during peak hours and access to properties will be maintained at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be temporarily unavailable. articles.title: Craigavon - Closure of Maple Path & Parkmore Footbridges
articles.description: Closure of Maple Path and Parkmore Footbridges, Craigavon The Department for Infrastructure have announced that the Maple Path and Parkmore footbridges in Craigavon will be closed from Thursday 4 June 2026. Detailed engineering inspections identified structural concerns, and it has been concluded that the closure of these footbridges is necessary while a permanent solution is developed. Alternative local walking routes are available and will be signposted where appropriate. While these routes may increase journey times for some users, they will provide access around the affected areas. The Department recognises the importance of both footbridges to local residents and apologises for any inconvenience caused. However, as the Department’s infrastructure assets age there will always be an eventual need to replace structures that present safety issues or have come to the end of their natural lifespan. Further information on future proposals for the bridges will be provided as work progresses. The Department would like to thank the public for their patience and cooperation.

articles.description: Schiff Bill Would Make Taxpayers Pay For Migrants' Housing, Food And Rehab While They Fight Deportation Sen. Adam Schiff's immigration bill would let the government-paid lawyers it creates for people facing deportation ask for public money to cover their clients' housing, food, travel, mental health care and addiction treatment , as War Room's Natalie Winters pointed out Monday. The Fairness to Freedom Act of 2026 (S. 5324) would create a federal right to a lawyer, at government expense, for anyone facing removal who can't afford one. A sworn statement that family income is no more than 200% of the poverty line is enough to qualify. articles.title: Election was a check on Trump — and Biden — foreign policy
articles.description: There is no debate as to why Donald Trump and the Republican Party suffered a historic and humiliating defeat at the polls on Tuesday: it all comes down to the Iran war and the cost-of-living crisis it has brought about. But lost in the conversation is that this was not just a rejection of the Iran war. It was also a repudiation of the broader foreign policy that repeatedly gets the U.S. into wars — or into supporting the wars and war crimes of U.S. partners. In many contests on Tuesday, the U.S.-Israel relationship was on the ballot too, and it was rejected by Republicans and Democrats alike in favor of recentering priorities back to national interests, including ending the flow of military aid to Israel. Trump famously ran on a promise to end forever wars and not to start new ones. But he ended up listening to the Israeli Prime Minister and started a major war with Iran, even though a diplomatic deal was on the table that was objectively stronger than President Barack Obama’s deal . Trump could have declared victory, but instead he listened to the Israeli government and chose to declare war. Now he is paying for it by losing his majority in Congress. articles.title: Neocons in full meltdown as voters punish GOP for Iran war
articles.description: It has long been claimed that Americans do not vote based on foreign policy, but the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections demonstrated the limits of this truism, with a large majority of voters rejecting the Iran War waged by the Trump administration. Even before the election, an October Fox News poll indicated that the Iran war and issues associated with it (inflation and gas prices) were among the top issues voters were concerned about. Exit polling published by NBC News showed 74% of voters saw the Iran war as a “crucial” or “major factor” in their vote, while 62% believed using force against Iran was the wrong decision. This apparently has come as a nasty surprise to the war’s biggest defenders and surrogates, who had assured their followers that this backlash would not happen. Some have admitted their errors, but many have not, and that split has rapidly produced a circular firing squad, with neocons aggressively turning on those in their ranks who have conceded the war was a mistake. articles.title: 2026 wasn't the first time war swayed an election
articles.description: If foreign policy could decide an election, then 1992 upended expectations. Barely eight months after the Soviet flag was lowered from the Kremlin for the last time, President George H. W. Bush found himself reminding Americans that he had led the USSR peacefully into history’s dustbin while also liberating Kuwait from the clutches of Saddam Hussein. “My opponents say I spend too much time on foreign policy, as if it didn't matter that schoolchildren once hid under their desks in drills to prepare for nuclear war,” said Bush during his acceptance speech at the 1992 Republican National Convention. “Over the past 4 years, more people have breathed the fresh air of freedom than in all of human history.” Foreign policy mattered to Bush. He was a combat pilot during the Second World War and later served as ambassador to the United Nations, CIA Director, and Ronald Reagan’s vice president. It mattered a lot less to voters angry about a sluggish economy and high unemployment: 73% said the country was on the wrong track in 1992. articles.description: US Closes The "Cloud Loophole": Days After Jensen's Exit, New Rule Puts AI Chip Rentals To China And Five "Diversion" Hubs Under License For four years, Washington has banned shipping America's best AI chips to China. For most of that time, Chinese labs have simply rented them instead. On Monday, the Commerce Department finally moved to shut that door , issuing an interim final rule that limits remote access to advanced AI chips and servers , a move Bloomberg tied directly to the "increased scrutiny over semiconductor exports after an alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia." The department's own framing: "The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries. " In other words, if you can't export the chip to Beijing, you can't export the compute either. And to make sure the point lands, the rule also slaps a license requirement on advanced AI chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil . *US ISSUES RULE RESTRICTING REMOTE ACCESS TO ADVANCED AI CHIPS — zerohedge (@zerohedge) November 16, 2026 The timing is

articles.title: Kalshi Quietly Bought A Broker As Democrats Prepare To Pounce
articles.description: Kalshi Quietly Bought A Broker As Democrats Prepare To Pounce Kalshi quietly bought a small broker-dealer in July and plans to launch stock trading within the next two months , the Wall Street Journal reported Monday. The firm, FB Securities, was set up in 2024 and is run by CEO John Rosanelli, according to Finra filings, and some of its employees are staying on with Kalshi. The prediction-markets platform plans to list stocks, exchange-traded funds and similar products as it builds itself into a multiasset exchange. Stocks are the next step in a push beyond yes-or-no event contracts into perpetual futures, the crypto-born derivative that never expires, trades around the clock and lets traders use leverage to magnify gains and losses. After rolling out perps on crypto, precious metals and commodities this year, Kalshi launched single-stock perpetual futures on Nov. 5, covering more than 50 companies including McDonald's, Palantir, SpaceX and Meta. Users traded more than $300 million of them on the first morning, co-founder and COO Luana Lopes Lara said . articles.title: Forensic Scientist Tells The NY Times Epstein Was Murdered
articles.description: Forensic Scientist Tells The NY Times Epstein Was Murdered A forensic scientist who spent a year going through Jeffrey Epstein's autopsy file argued in London on Monday that Epstein's injuries are most plausibly explained by homicidal strangulation, not the suicidal hanging New York City's medical examiner ruled in 2019. Michael Freeman, a professor of forensic medicine and editor-in-chief of the Journal of Forensic and Legal Medicine , told the New York Times his first thought on seeing one photo from the autopsy was: "Wait a minute, that doesn't look like a hanging mark." A textbook hanging leaves a smooth, even line that slants up to a peak. The mark on Epstein's neck, as Freeman describes it, was deep and ragged and forked into a Y on one side. A cropped portion of a photo from the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner, depicting ligature wounds on Jeffrey Epstein's neck. CBS News  Freeman laid out his case at the Middle Temple, one of London's legal societies. He argues the body also carries signs of a struggle that the medical examiner's findings did not account for. articles.description: Supreme Court To Consider Trump's Asylum Restrictions At Southern Border Authored by Jack Phillips via The Epoch Times , The U.S. Supreme Court on Friday agreed to take up a case challenging whether President Donald Trump's administration has the authority to bar asylum applications from people who cross into the United States from the southern border. Right after he took office on Jan. 20, 2025, Trump signed a proclamation restricting people who cross the southern border without authorization from seeking asylum, one of a series of immigration restrictions that the president rolled out soon after he was sworn in. It has remained in place amid litigation. In agreeing to take up the case, the Supreme Court is likely to render a decision on it at the end of its term in June or July 2027. The Trump administration, in court filings, has written that it wants to overturn lower court decisions that found the proclamation illegal . Trump's asylum policy is one of a number of measures his administration has taken as part of a crackdown on illegal immigration that the president has pursued since returning to office last year. articles.title: Once-Bitter Rivals Forge The Most "Consequential" Alliance Of Trump's Second Term
articles.description: Once-Bitter Rivals Forge The Most "Consequential" Alliance Of Trump's Second Term Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller have gone from bitter political enemies to powerful allies , forging what The Wall Street Journal describes as "one of the most under-the-radar - and consequential - " partnerships of President Donald Trump's second term. Rubio was a leading member of the bipartisan "Gang of Eight" senators who crafted an immigration overhaul in 2013 that included a pathway to citizenship for millions of illegal immigrants. The legislation passed the Senate but died in the Republican-controlled House, becoming a major liability for Rubio among conservatives and later haunting his 2016 presidential campaign. In 2015, Miller privately urged Breitbart News staffers to publish negative coverage of Rubio over his support for bipartisan immigration reform , according to messages that became public in 2019. articles.title: She gets 16 pelvic exams a day – so yours don’t hurt
articles.description: Molly Callahan, a gynecological teaching assistant, helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams On her busiest days, Molly Callahan, has 16 speculums inserted into her vagina. She works full-time as a gynecological teaching assistant ( GTA ) – a layperson who helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams before they work with actual patients. It’s not as unpleasant as you might think. In fact, the point is to help students learn how to do it without causing discomfort. articles.title: ‘Seduced by a dramatic landscape of canyons and lakes’: exploring Catalonia’s wild side
articles.description: A historic single-track train line through the foothills of the Pyrenees opens up a pristine wilderness of forests, gorges and thundering rivers Alighting at the train station of Santa Linya in northern Spain, I paused to wonder what the railway engineers were thinking. A rough halt hewn out of the mountainside, with no ticket office, no waiting room, no sign of human habitation – just a single platform in the wilderness. On the far side of the track, a shimmering turquoise lake flanked by pine forests. Ahead – the only way out – a rocky trail snaking up the limestone cliff. My husband and I had first strayed into this western corner of Catalonia – Pallars Jussà – on our honeymoon road trip 21 years earlier. Seduced by its dramatic landscape of canyons, lakes, crumbling ruins and the formidable Noguera Pallaresa river thundering south from the Pyrenees, we had vowed to return one day. He loves mountains, I love water, we both love abandoned buildings; it was a geographical match made in heaven. Now those vows had come good – we were back, on a mission to go deeper into the hinterland. Continue reading...

articles.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
articles.description: Ulster Hall, Belfast With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers ‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage. They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever. Continue reading...

A renewed push by proponents of carbon dioxide removal (or CDR), where heat-trapping carbon dioxide is taken from the atmosphere and stored deep underground, in oceans or in products such as carbonated drinks, is seeking to gain recognition in the final text of Cop31, the climate summit currently under way in Antalya, Turkey. articles.title: Ma Wee Tin O’Shortbreid: a journey in search of the real Highlands
articles.description: Ma Wee Tin o’ Shortbreid began as a cautionary note: don’t make the Highlands look like a shortbread tin. Then Dougie Wallace shot a Chinese tourist beneath a wee umbrella, and the warning became the title Growing up in Scotland, our family was one of many who kept their photographs in an old shortbread tin. The lid usually showed a castle beside a loch, a stag, a Highland coo and plenty of tartan. It was always sunny. Ma Wee Tin o’ Shortbreid is Scots for “my little tin of shortbread”. The title started as a warning to myself: don’t make the Highlands look like a tin of shortbread. Isle of Mull. Out of the camper van, looking for white-tailed eagles. They were shot to extinction in Britain, the last one in Shetland in 1918. Brought back from Norway in the 1970s. Now they are one of the island’s biggest draws. A bird once shot on sight is part of the sales pitch. The Scotland on the lid promises wilderness and wildlife. The real one comes with binoculars and a long wait. Continue reading...

articles.title: TV tonight: Nicola Coughlan and Joe Cole’s powerful drama about a toxic relationship
articles.description: The two stars are brilliant in Dominic Savage’s I Am Helen. Plus: Wayne Rooney and a bunch of celebrities land in the jungle. Steve wants to get married and have children; Helen is still undecided. But that’s not all. Steve is bored by the sex they have, too. And he’d rather Helen didn’t pursue her career dreams. There’s also a workmate who is whispering ideas into his ear. As Helen and Steve’s relationship unravels, so, too, does a compelling exploration of toxic masculinity and its poisoning of relationships. articles.title: The Nice Ones review – invasion of the sunny personality snatchers
articles.description: Peter Stylianou’s watchably unsettling tale of unbalanced minds and Unidentified Aerial Phenomena does its best to please Drone shots are two-a-penny in cinema these days, but it’s a mark of this £80,000 British indie sci-fi’s visual astuteness that it largely avoids them in a film plagued by drone-like entities. Instead, it takes a suggestive approach: protagonist Kate (Joelle Rae) is staring out of the window on a car journey, up into the night sky, when a pinprick of light flares out before shooting out a laser towards the ground – then darting off into a cloudbank. Kate chews over this anomaly with boyfriend Dale (Emrhys Cooper), en route to a get-together of his old uni gang in a countryside Airbnb. Already not at ease among his mates, Kate gets a ribbing when she repeats her UFO story (or Unidentified Aerial Phenomena, as they are called these days). And there are knowing glances about her psychiatric history: she once fended off an abusive boyfriend at knifepoint, insisting he was possessed. articles.title: ‘Partly the movie’s fault I’m a writer at all’: why Wonder Boys is my feelgood movie
articles.description: The latest in our series of writers picking their most comforting rewatches is a tribute to Curtis Hanson’s insightful 2000 comedy drama I’m allergic to movies and books about writers. Washed-up novelists, aspiring screenwriters, creative writing professors in the throes of a midlife crisis who cheat on their wives – take your pick. Chalk it up to my being a writer who for two decades wrote continually and fruitlessly about writers. And yet, I love Wonder Boys, Curtis Hanson’s 2000 comedy drama about a rumpled creative writing professor who can’t seem to finish his second novel and is having an affair with his boss’s wife. It’s partly the movie’s fault I’m a writer at all. I saw Wonder Boys on its opening weekend, when I was 17, and the notion of poring over novels with kindred spirits in a sun-dappled seminar room at some leafy liberal arts college – where I’d find myself a year later – held endless appeal. Even the misadventures of the film’s professor, Grady Tripp (Michael Douglas, never better), seemed romantic to me. On the eve of his university’s annual literary festival, Grady’s wife leaves him. His lover, Sara, announces she’s pregnant with his child. And James Leer, his br

articles.title: Not All Those Who Wander Are Lost album review – Anna Lapwood journeys to middle earth
articles.description: Lapwood/Nidaros Cathedral Girls’ Choir (Sony) Lapwood has turned Howard Shore’s film score into an impressive full-blown organ symphony When a fan requested she play Concerning Hobbits from The Lord of the Rings, little did Anna Lapwood imagine that she would go on to spend a year turning Howard Shore’s leitmotif-led soundtrack into a full-blown organ symphony. Remarkably, she transcribed all but one segment by ear, a feat in itself. That she manages to tell the story chronologically over a 38-minute, three-movement span is equally impressive. But wait, there’s more. Reckoning the symphony would benefit from the human voice, she incorporated a handful of songs, performing them live – in Tolkien’s Elvish dialect – while playing the Nidaros Cathedral organ in Trondheim, Norway. The results are frequently convincing, though the folksy music of the Shire is less effective on the organ than the baleful music of Sauron and the Ringwraiths. The latter in particular captures the sounds we associate with Widor, Boëllmann and Vierne in full gothic overdrive. If anything, Lapwood could afford to let rip more often, though her finger- and foot-work shine, as do the ethereal voices of the Nidar

articles.title: The Sensualist by Gary Shteyngart review – a delectable romp through life’s pleasures
articles.description: From martinis to capybara videos, the novelist celebrates the little things (some more expensive than others) that bring him joy In 2024, the novelist Gary Shteyngart flew from New York to Milan in search of the perfect midnight-blue suit. There he chose fabric, before flying to Hong Kong to be fitted for four shirts, and on to Tokyo, where he was measured by master tailor Yuhei Yamamoto and master shoe­maker Yohei Fukuda. A short king (“five foot five and a half, with that ‘half’ doing a lot of work”), Shteyngart dreamed of a fit to disappear his 52-year-old moobs (“my tatas”, “my chimichangas”) and melt the heart of the toughest maitre d’ at the most in-demand restaurants. And guess what? The world’s finest craftsmen will give you all that – though Shteyngart, who emigrated from Leningrad to the US in 1979, argues that a great suit serves a deeper need than vanity. Trying it on two days after Trump’s second election, “it was the final certificate of naturalization … I couldn’t make my adopted country fall out of love with fascism, but at least I could enjoy my new shoes.” Clothes become an advanced form of self-care. Continue reading...

articles.title: Post your questions for A-ha frontman Morten Harket
articles.description: As he releases new solo album Human Grace, and lives with Parkinson’s disease, the synthpop heartthrob will take on your questions His group A-ha were one of the defining acts of 80s synthpop, thanks to hits such as Take On Me and Hunting High and Low – and lead singer Morten Harket is now about to release one of the most poignant albums of his career. As he does so, he’ll be joining us to answer your questions. Born and raised in Norway where he still lives, Harket struck out for London in 1982 with his bandmates Paul Waaktaar-Savoy and Magne Furuholmen, determined to make it in the music business. They had a killer opening gambit with Take On Me – which climaxed with Harket’s startlingly pristine falsetto singing. After a couple of failed releases, it finally hit the big time in 1985, topping charts all over the world including in the US: the first Norwegian band to do so there. Continue reading...

articles.description: Pattinson is a character actor whose talent for inscrutable appraisal may mean a new era for 007. Will this more willowy, classy Bond leave sexism in the shadows? • New James Bond announced ... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson • Share your thoughts on the casting • Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to James Bond If it wasn’t Bond … maybe it would have been Dr No in some hi-tech reboot. But Robert Pattinson – with his movie-star chops and track record in hip A24-type character turns, and his gift for cool, inscrutable appraisal and sensual menace – is an exquisite choice as 007, playing on the darker and more sophisticated notes of Pattinson’s performing personality. And let’s hope, incidentally, that the actor now isn’t forced into a five-hour daily gym regimen to bulk up. I like the taller and more willowy Bond that Pattinson represents, the Bond from whose frame the tux hangs gracefully, the Bond with elegant abandon who’s a former British Naval officer, not a former US Navy Seal, the Bond who with a crinkly-eyed reptilian grin can style out waking up with a hangover after too many whisky-and-sodas at the baccarat table. articles.title: Hero, villain or victim: why are refugees so rarely seen now as fully human? | Zoe Williams
articles.description: The understanding of refugees as complex individuals, motivated variously by wanting to build a new life and return to what was theirs, often seems to have been lost. A new film offers a different, truer, perspective There was a screening last week of Seize the Summit, which follows four refugees as they try to reach the top of Kilimanjaro. It was organised by a recent MA graduate from Goldsmiths, with a panel afterwards, which I was set to chair. So she and I were spitballing what the film-maker, Arwa Damon, would want to talk about, and Hanya, the graduate, said: “I think her purpose is to mainstream the idea of the refugee as a human being.” It was such a stark statement that we both started laughing. There are many categories of refugee in current affairs storytelling. There’s the desperate victim; the criminal, or criminal-waiting-to-happen; the hero, battling unimaginable odds, though this tends to be a retrospective narrative, ie second-generation members of a diaspora talking about their parents. There are refugees en masse, shorn of any traits or qualities at all, discussed purely in terms of whether or not the host state can accommodate them, and how long they should be a

articles.title: The hill I will die on: There is only one acceptable occasion on which to ghost someone – when you die | Temi Wilkey
articles.description: Dystopian dating on apps is more Thatcherite horror story than love story. Romance that blossoms through community and human connection needs a renaissance Digitising our dating lives has conditioned us all away from human connection. I spend weeks of my life huffing and puffing to keep the balloon of flirty banter in the air – with a stranger I only find vaguely attractive. I go on dates with people who are “my type on paper” but upon meeting, find the paper much better than the person. I meet a woman with a devastating mouth and an even more devastating wit, only for her to ghost . The only acceptable reason to ghost someone is if you have, in fact, died. Long ago, when Margaret Thatcher proclaimed “There is no such thing as society”, she wasn’t heralding an era of Tory rule that destroyed all public services that kept true community alive. No – she was prophesying 40 years into the future about the digital-age phenomenon of ghosting. The fact that this practice is widespread enough for there to be a word for it is proof of the long since disintegrated fabric of our society. Temi Wilkey is a writer, performer and star of the one-woman shows Main Character Energy and Lover Girl ,

articles.title: Not ready for the cold and dark? Maybe you need a ‘winter transition week’ | Emma Beddington
articles.description: A psychologist has recommended we all take time for slowness and rest, to prepare ourselves for the coming months. It’s a nice idea, but it may prove my downfall How are you feeling about the rapid dying of the light? Are you already sluggish and glum, poleaxed by the “polar vortex” or seasonal lurgy? That might be because you’re doing winter wrong: according to health psychologist Kari Leibowitz, writing in the Washington Post , we’d all benefit from a “winter transition week”. Leibowitz, the author of a book, How to Winter , based on her time living in the Arctic, explains: “I intentionally clear out my calendar … say no to extra obligations, try to cancel or postpone unnecessary meetings and make time for rest and slowness.” During this time, she also recommends stocking up on tea, getting out thick socks, eating soup and planning little treats. articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Mr Baxter, who ate our belongings – and broke our hearts
articles.description: Reared on a puppy farm, and abandoned by a previous owner, he was half-starved when we adopted him. But he grew strong, chomping through everything from dog beds to sunglasses and my debut book The day we brought our 14-week-old cocker spaniel home in 2022, I was wearing a silk scarf I’d picked up decades ago in a vintage shop in Tokyo. I didn’t know it then but that rainy afternoon would be the last time I’d wear it. Three days later, it was in my new puppy’s mouth. Once he’d finished tearing my scarf to shreds, he gazed at me with soulful chocolate brown eyes, fluttering his long eyelashes. No matter how fond I was of that silk scarf, how could I be angry? Puppies chew stuff. That’s what they do. Mr Baxter gnawed his way through four dog beds, blankets and multiple dog leads. Nothing was off-limits. Socks, shoes, trainers, gloves, flat caps, berets, the freshly printed chapters of my debut book, a nifty pair of 70s sunglasses. Fearless and lithe, he grabbed things we naively thought were out of reach, and woe betide anyone who tried to take them from him. Continue reading...

And, when I got it, that job was my gateway to Melbourne. I’d just moved and suddenly my life was brimming with cool and clever people, recommendations for art, music and food, and a dizzying number of expensive skincare products, stashed haphazardly in my share house bathroom. articles.title: A Dark Storm Is Gathering Over The Housing Market
articles.description: A Dark Storm Is Gathering Over The Housing Market Submitted by QTR's Fringe Finance I’ve been warning about the continued risks surrounding AI steadily since August , and I continue to believe we’re going to see more bad news from the sector that has driven the bull market of the last few years.  I also think more bad news is coming for Nvidia and I’ve also warned about crypto , and the shaky price action we saw this weekend reinforces my view that more volatility and downside could be ahead. I know, it’s a downer for a Sunday morning. And spoiler alert: today’s column isn’t going to be bright and cheery, either. Hey…if I have to suffer on Sundays as an Eagles fan this year, I’m insisting you must suffer, too. articles.title: "Highest Risk Will Be This Winter": Regulators From 38 Countries Warn Of Nuclear Accident In Ukraine
articles.description: "Highest Risk Will Be This Winter": Regulators From 38 Countries Warn Of Nuclear Accident In Ukraine Nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries warned Monday that the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is rising this winter , and called on Russia to stop striking the power grid that Ukraine's reactors need to keep their fuel cool, according to a joint statement seen by Reuters before its release. The statement comes from three European bodies, HERCA, WENRA and NORA, whose members cover every EU country plus the US, Britain, Canada and Japan. The regulators "express our deep concern about the increasing risks to nuclear safety arising from Russia's war against Ukraine," and said they see "an urgent need for Russia to cease attacks against Ukraine's nuclear facilities" and the energy infrastructure those plants depend on. Without a stable grid supply, Ukraine's nuclear plants find it harder to keep nuclear material cool and avoid a meltdown , the regulators said: the kind of meltdown that made Chernobyl in 1986 the world's worst civil nuclear accident, spreading iodine-131, cesium-134 and cesium-137 across Ukraine, Belarus, Russia and much of northern and central Europe.

In its latest monthly report, published on Friday, the agency said that global oil supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day (mb/d) in October to 105.4 mb/d . The climb followed a 3 mb/d increase in September. "The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said. The agency forecast that the market would return to a supply surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, with a larger build expected in 2027 . But the agency warned that fuel markets remain under severe pressure, particularly for diesel, and its member countries are accelerating the release of emergency stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel, to bridge the gap. articles.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
articles.description: Bristol Beacon The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things. Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun ’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor. Continue reading...

It is a feeling that is very unusual when you have about 85 people working in the domestic violence sector gathered in one room. articles.title: Squabble over leadership risks plunging the OSCE into crisis
articles.description: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) is staring down the barrel of entering 2027 without a chair for the first time in its 51-year history. The Europeans are wrestling Turkey to drop its veto over Cyprus’ bid, raising the stakes by loudly opposing the only other candidate, Georgia. Unable to win over Ankara, Europe should drop its objections to Tbilisi to avert a crisis. With three weeks to go until the OSCE Ministerial Council in Lugano, Switzerland, on December 3, the organization remains deadlocked over who should lead it from 2027-28. The chairperson-in-office role rotates every two years and is normally voted on well in advance with agreement by consensus. EU member Cyprus was the first country to put its hat in the ring almost two years ago, in December 2024. However, Cyprus’ bid has been vetoed by Turkey on the basis of the long-standing dispute over the division of the island in 1974 . There is a long history of enmity over the issue between NATO members Turkey and Greece, the latter of which has long backed Cyprus and opposed Turkey’s occupation of half of the island. articles.title: Nvidia Lacks Corporate D&O Insurance Amid Huang Scandal
articles.description: Nvidia Lacks Corporate D&O Insurance Amid Huang Scandal Nvidia does not have directors’ and officers’ (D&O) liability insurance covering the company itself, an unusual omission for a major US-listed corporation that could leave the chipmaker facing substantial legal costs amid the controversy surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang, according to Financial Times . The FT writes that while Nvidia reportedly maintains $900mn in insurance protecting its directors and senior executives from personal liability, the policy does not extend to the company’s own financial exposure. The coverage, arranged through Aon and involving insurers including Beazley, AIG and Chubb, is limited to what the industry calls Side A protection. Most large publicly traded US companies also purchase Side B and Side C insurance, which can reimburse corporate legal expenses and cover certain claims brought directly against the company. Nvidia’s decision to operate without these protections is uncommon, although high premiums can lead some businesses to retain such risks themselves. The insurance gap has gained attention following Huang’s abrupt resignation and a subsequent shareholder lawsuit. Investors

articles.description: Reactor Developers Line Up For Uranium Enrichment From Centrus Meta's money has found its way to the nuclear fuel chain , as Oklo has lined up uranium enrichment services from Centrus for its reactor plant in Ohio. On November 12, Oklo said it signed "multiple definitive, multi-year contracts" with Centrus Energy for high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU), formalizing a letter of intent from June. The disclosed terms: Enough HALEU for "up to five Aurora powerhouses for multiple years," the first phase of Oklo's planned 1.2 GW campus in Pike County, Ohio. Deliveries from Centrus's plant in Piketon, "scheduled to begin in 2029." Oklo prepays for the fuel, which helps fund Centrus's build-out. Meta's prepayment for future power, which we flagged in January, helps pay for it. The fuel also covers future Aurora projects and, eventually, refueling Oklo's first reactor in Idaho. Oklo isn't the only one lining up enrichment services. Since August, Centrus has signed three more definitive deals for the same future output, all with prepayments: X-energy (Aug. 6): enrichment for LEU and HALEU for its first Xe-100 reactors and TRISO-X fuel.
